mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during periods of FEDFUNDS > 4%, or the S&P 500 20-day return is positive despite the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE exceeding 0.2 percentage points coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as lower expected future wage growth reduces equity risk premia.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by more than 0.2pp in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or insignificant when UNRATE rises >0.2pp, or the effect is not significant in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) of at least 2% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals a bottom in supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls at least 2% for two consecutive months then rises above previous month's value
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return after such a pattern, or the pattern is not followed by a rebound.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO exceeds 102 (2017=100 index) for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to over-supply in the economy depressing growth expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive during such an INDPRO pattern, or the effect is not robust across multiple cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained dual decline in both FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 (quarterly GDP) for two consecutive quarters predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher rates and weak demand jointly depress equity valuations.
regime_hint: Concurrent monetary tightening and weak demand
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive or not significantly negative when both triggers are present, or interaction term is insignificant in regression.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS falls by more than 10,000 monthly for two consecutive months (indicating job losses), the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to be negative due to rising labor market uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >10,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is positive despite the trigger, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly surge in RSAFS (retail sales) above 5,000 million dollars followed by a sustained level above 6,000 million for the next month predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals consumer demand strength.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5,000M for one month and >6,000M in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day return is negative or insignificant when the pattern occurs, or the effect is not robust in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE and HOUST both show improving labor market conditions (UNRATE rises >0.1pp and HOUST increases >2% in the same month), the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as dual improvements reduce recession risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases >0.1pp AND HOUST increases >2% in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return when both proxies improve jointly, or interaction is not statistically significant.
